title: Family petition (Form I-130) for a spouse: documents needed
use_when: The client is a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident petitioning for a husband or wife on Form I-130.
note: Based on the USCIS Instructions for Form I-130 and I-130A (edition 04/01/24). The responsible lawyer decides what the matter needs.

i130-instr.name: USCIS, Instructions for Form I-130, Petition for Alien Relative, and Form I-130A, edition 04/01/24

situations.petitioner-citizen: Is the petitioner a U.S. citizen?
situations.petitioner-lpr: Is the petitioner a lawful permanent resident (green card holder)?
situations.spouse-in-us: Is the spouse being petitioned for in the United States?
situations.heightened-proof: Did the marriage take place while the spouse was in exclusion, deportation, removal or rescission proceedings, or did a permanent resident petitioner get residence through an earlier marriage and remarry within five years?
situations.name-change: Does the petitioner or the spouse use a name different from the one on their documents?
situations.foreign-language: Are any documents in a language other than English?

items.label: Proof the petitioner is a U.S. citizen (one of the documents listed)
items.detail: A copy of a birth certificate issued by a civil registrar, vital statistics office, or other civil authority showing birth in the United States; a copy of a naturalization certificate or certificate of citizenship; a copy of Form FS-240, Consular Report of Birth Abroad; a copy of an unexpired U.S. passport; or an original statement from a U.S. consular officer verifying U.S. citizenship with a valid passport. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Copy of the front and back of the petitioner's Permanent Resident Card (Form I-551)
items.detail: If the card has not yet been received: copies of the passport biographic page and the page showing admission as a lawful permanent resident, or other evidence of permanent resident status issued by USCIS or the former INS. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Documents showing each prior marriage legally ended
items.detail: Copies of documents showing that each of the prior marriages of either spouse was legally terminated.

items.label: Form I-130A, Supplemental Information for Spouse Beneficiary, completed and signed by the spouse
items.detail: If the spouse is overseas, Form I-130A must still be completed, but the spouse does not have to sign it.

items.label: Two identical color passport-style photographs of the petitioner
items.detail: Taken within 30 days of filing the petition. 2 by 2 inches, in color, full face, frontal view, white to off-white background, printed on thin paper with a glossy finish, unmounted and unretouched.

items.label: Two identical color passport-style photographs of the spouse
items.detail: Taken within 30 days of filing the petition. 2 by 2 inches, in color, full face, frontal view, white to off-white background, printed on thin paper with a glossy finish, unmounted and unretouched. Required if the spouse is in the United States.

sections.name: Evidence the marriage is genuine (one or more)

items.label: Documentation showing joint ownership of property
Lease showing joint tenancy of a common residence
items.detail: Meaning both spouses live at the same address together.

items.label: Documentation showing the spouses have combined their financial resources
items.detail: Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Birth certificates of children born to the spouses together
Affidavits from third parties with personal knowledge of the marriage
items.detail: Sworn to or affirmed. Each affidavit must contain the full name and address of the person making it; that person's date and place of birth; and complete information and details explaining how the person acquired his or her knowledge of the marriage.

items.label: Any other relevant documentation that there is an ongoing marital union
Additional evidence that the marriage was entered into in good faith and not for immigration purposes
items.detail: The instructions require clear and convincing evidence in these situations; they do not list specific documents.

items.label: Legal documents showing the name change
items.detail: Copies of the legal documents reflecting the name change, such as a marriage certificate, adoption decree, or court order, if the petitioner or the relative uses a name different from the one on the relevant documents.

items.label: Full English translation of every foreign-language document
items.detail: The translator must sign a certification that the English translation is complete and accurate and that he or she is competent to translate from the foreign language into English.
